entities.summary:
Bartolomeo Borghesi (unknown–April 16, 1860) was a prominent Italian antiquarian who played a pivotal role in establishing the science of numismatics.



As a leading figure in the field, Borghesi excavated numerous archaeological sites in Italy and Europe, uncovering an array of ancient coins that shed new light on the economic and cultural systems of ancient civilizations. His work at the Palatine Hill in Rome uncovered the remains of the Roman imperial mint, significantly contributing to the understanding of the Roman Empire's economic policies.



Borghesi's research and discoveries had a lasting impact on the field of numismatics, influencing generations of scholars and shaping the development of modern numismatic theory. The establishment of the Italian Numismatic Society in 1861, which Borghesi co-founded, further solidified his reputation as a leading authority in the field.



His work also extended beyond the realm of numismatics, with Borghesi's excavations at the ancient Greek city of Paestum in southern Italy revealing significant insights into the cultural and artistic achievements of ancient Greece.



Borghesi's legacy extends beyond his own contributions, as his work paved the way for future generations of archaeologists, historians, and scholars to explore the rich cultural heritage of the ancient world.
